name: Pinochle Three Player
description: Three-player Pinochle: each plays for themselves. Deal 15 cards each and a 3-card kitty. Auction to name trump (min 20, or 19 for dealer); high bidder takes the kitty, declares trump, and all meld. Fifteen tricks; follow suit, trump when void. First to 100 points wins. Must take at least one trick to count meld; fail contract costs the bid amount.

overview.description: Three-player Pinochle: each plays for themselves. Deal 15 cards each and a 3-card kitty. history.origins: Pinochle descends from the European game Bezique, either as a cousin of Binokel or directly from the Swiss and South German game Binocle (Binokel), which is itself a descendant of Bezique. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where the name was mispronounced and misspelled as pinochle. The game became a favorite among American Jewish and Irish immigrants. The three-player auction variant developed in the United States; its bidding has similarities to German Skat and to bid whist. During World War I the game was briefly outlawed in Syracuse, New York, and some other US cities due to anti-German sentiment, but it has since regained broad popularity.
timeline: Late 19th century: German immigrants brought Binokel to America; game adopted and renamed Pinochle. Three-player auction variant developed in the US.

setup.players: Three players; each plays for themselves.
setup.deck: 48-card Pinochle deck (two copies of 9 through Ace in each of four suits).
setup.dealing: Dealer deals 15 cards to each player and 3 cards to the kitty (middle). Deal rotates clockwise; packets of three or four at a time, starting with player to dealer's left.

rules.objective: Be the first to reach 100 points by bidding, melding, and taking tricks. Each hand: auction to name trump, meld for points, then play 15 tricks. Bid winner must make their contract (meld plus trick points) or lose the bid amount.
rules.gameplay: Dealer deals 15 cards to each player and 3 to the kitty. Player to dealer's left opens bidding (minimum 20, or 19 if dealer); bids increase by 1. With meld, opening player must bid or pass passes obligation. Highest bidder takes the kitty, declares trump, and all three show melds. Bid winner discards 3 cards to reduce to 15; melds return to hands. High bidder leads; follow suit when possible, trump when void. Must take at least one trick to count meld. Trick points plus bid winner's three discards total 25; bidder must meet contract or score minus the bid.
keyRules: Auction: bid or pass, minimum 20 (19 for dealer)
Bid winner takes kitty, declares trump, discards 3
All meld; bid winner leads; follow suit, must overtake when able (or house rules)

variations.name: Cutthroat
variations.description: No kitty. Deal entire deck: 16 cards each. Win only by bidding and making contract to reach winning score; high score without a winning bid does not win.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only deal size and win condition; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Check
variations.description: Gambling variant; same as to 100 but players track checks (e.g. stakes). Flush/run, aces, roundtable earn checks; looking at talon and losing costs checks; double marriage, double pinochle, double arounds earn extra.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Check variant adds stakes and scoring rules; engine structure unchanged.

scoring.description: Meld points (runs, marriages, pinochle, dix, arounds) plus trick points (aces 11, tens 10, kings 4, queens 3, jacks 2, nines 0; last trick 10). Bid winner's three discards count toward their trick total. Total trick points 25 per hand. If bidder fails contract, score minus the bid and meld cancelled.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach 100 points wins. Ties: play another hand, or extend to 125 then 150, or high bidder on that hand wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Pinochle for three players; auction; melding and trick-taking.
